extracted.intended_audience: readers of Benjamin Franklin's letters; students and general readers of 18th-century correspondence
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria are practical, moral, and procedural recommendations embedded in Benjamin Franklin's personal letters (advice on trade, household, reading, marriage, public conduct, and politics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to appearances in conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Appearances should therefore be attended to in our conduct towards them as well as relatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: People in certain circumstances are apt to suspect without cause; therefore be mindful of outward conduct and appearances toward such persons to avoid misunderstandings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquire a habit of industry with a trade
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade is a valuable thing; but unless a habit of industry be acquired with it, it turns out of little use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical success in a trade depends not merely on learning the trade but on cultivating industrious habits; training and consistent diligence make the trade profitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wife's industry and frugality as household fortune
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry, frugality, and prudent economy in a wife, are to a tradesman, in their effects, a fortune; and a fortune sufficient for Benjamin, if his expectations are reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing a marriage partner for a tradesman, value practical household management and thriftiness as equivalent to a financial dowry; they create economic security over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure product quality; avoid deceiving by appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: I hope he will always take care to make it faithfully, never slight manufacture, or attempt to deceive by appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only produce goods of true quality; do not rely on superficial appearance or deceptive presentation. High-quality manufacture enables confident use of one's name and mark and builds reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use authentic trademarks; avoid counterfeit arms
rubrics_metrics.description: In his advertisements he may value himself on serving his time with the original maker, but put his own mark or device on the papers, or anything he may be advised as proper; only on the soap, as it is called by the name of crown soap, it seems necessary to use a stamp of that sort, and perhaps no soapboiler in the king's dominions has a better right to the crown than himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When advertising and branding, acknowledge training with reputable makers but use your own mark; avoid imitating or counterfeiting others' arms (which looks like attempted counterfeiting). Use any special stamp only if legitimately warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send samples only if they are truly good
rubrics_metrics.description: Let a box be sent to her (but not unless it be right good), and she will immediately return the ready money for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When soliciting support or business from family/agents, send only genuinely good product samples; good quality will secure payment and reputation, poor quality will harm prospects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask leave before taking others' property; respect due
rubrics_metrics.description: Nobody has wrote a syllable to me concerning his making use of the hammer... It was irregular, and if you had not approved of his doing it I should have thought it indiscreet. _Leave_, they say, is _light_, and it seems to me a piece of respect that was due to his aunt to ask it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect property and social obligations by asking permission before taking or using another's tools or goods; failure to do so is indiscreet and shows disrespect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfect honesty required in susceptible trades
rubrics_metrics.description: There is one accomplishment without which he cannot possibly thrive in that trade (i. e., _to be perfectly honest_). ... if a man is once detected in the smallest fraud it soon becomes public, and every one is put upon their guard against him; ... so at once he is ruined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In trades liable to suspicion (e.g., goldsmithing), absolute honesty is essential: even a small fraud destroys trust and livelihood. Establish character as honest, faithful, and skilful to secure employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer merit and regularity over favoritism in appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a rule with me not to remove any officer that behaves well, keeps regular accounts, and pays duly; and I think the rule is founded on reason and justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering personnel changes, do not remove well-behaved, accountable, and dutiful officers to satisfy personal resentments; base removals on conduct and competence, not family pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor reconciliation and forgiveness in family disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Above all things, I dislike family quarrels; and when they happen among my relations, nothing gives me more pain. ... I wish you were reconciled, and that I will love that side best that is most ready to forgive and oblige the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In family disagreements prefer reconciliation; be disposed to forgive and oblige. When judging distant quarrels, give weight to the side most willing to reconcile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active reading with notes to imprint learning
rubrics_metrics.description: I would advise you to read with a pen in your hand, and enter in a little book short hints of what you find that is curious or that may be useful; for this will be the best method of imprinting such particulars in your memory...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To learn and retain reading material, actively take brief notes of curious or useful points in a small notebook; this aids memory, future practical use, and enhances conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep and consult a good dictionary while reading
rubrics_metrics.description: I think it would be well for you to have a good dictionary at hand, to consult immediately when you meet with a word you do not comprehend the precise meaning of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult unfamiliar terms immediately to improve comprehension; the inconvenience decreases as vocabulary grows and reading becomes more satisfying and efficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask mentors for further information and book referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: When any point occurs in which you would be glad to have farther information than your book affords you, I beg you would not in the least apprehend that I should think it a trouble to receive and answer your questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a text leaves questions, seek guidance from knowledgeable correspondents or mentors, who can answer or direct you to appropriate books; asking is encouraged and seen as a pleasure rather than a burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political criterion: fair and equal representation for stable union
rubrics_metrics.description: I am fully persuaded with you, that a _consolidating union_, by a fair and equal representation of all the parts of this empire in Parliament, is the only firm basis on which its political grandeur and prosperity can be founded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For durable political union between distant parts of an empire, adopt fair and equal representation in the central legislature; failure to do so sours relations and risks separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative principle: assemblies should not be compelled to enact particular laws
rubrics_metrics.description: But to enjoin it to make a particular law, contrary to its own judgment, seems improper; an assembly or parliament not being an _executive_ officer of government, whose duty it is, in law-making, to obey orders, but a _deliberative_ body...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A superior legislature may have limits: compelling a subordinate deliberative assembly to pass a law against its judgment undermines the nature of deliberative government and is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal taxation without representation will be objected to
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal taxes laid on them by Parliament are still, and ever will be, objected to for the reason that you will see in the mentioned examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect internal taxes imposed by a distant legislature to provoke resistance when the taxed people lack representation; this is a persistent political grievance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer oxen to horses for agricultural economy
rubrics_metrics.description: I have observed in America that the farmers are more thriving in those parts of the country where horned cattle are used, than in those where the labour is done by horses. The latter are said to require twice the quantity of land to maintain them and, after all, are not good to eat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For agricultural efficiency, favor oxen over horses because horses consume more land for upkeep and are less useful as food; this affects population and subsistence capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure labour value by food production
rubrics_metrics.description: Food is _always_ necessary to _all_, and much the greatest part of the labour of mankind is employed in raising provisions for the mouth. Is not this kind of labour, then, the fittest to be the standard by which to measure the values of all other labour...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the labour required to produce subsistence (food) as a practical standard for comparing and valuing other kinds of labour and commodities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advocate early marriage for better mutual adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: I am rather inclined to think that early ones stand the best chance of happiness. The temper and habits of the young are not yet become so stiff and uncomplying as when more advanced in life; they form more easily to each other...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early marriage can produce better mutual adaptation and benefits (child-rearing, forming of habits), though particular circumstances may make delay prudent in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic conduct: respect, studiousness, industry, frugality, temperance, and virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat your wife always with respect; ... Never use a slighting expression to her, even in jest; ... Be studious in your profession, and you will be learned. Be industrious and frugal, and you will be rich. Be sober and temperate, and you will be healthy. Be in general virtuous, and you will be happy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For personal and domestic success, combine respectful behavior toward a spouse with professional study, industry, frugality, sobriety, temperance, and general virtue—these habits lead to respect, learning, wealth, health, and happiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soften public messaging by providing an honorable rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: If our people should follow the Boston example in entering into resolutions of frugality and industry, full as necessary for us as for them, I hope they will, among other things, give this reason, that 'tis to enable them more speedily and effectually to discharge their debts to Great Britain; this will soften a little, and, at the same time, appear honourable, and like ourselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When engaging in public political or economic demonstrations that may alarm others, frame the action with an honorable and conciliatory rationale to soften reactions and win favor—this is a pragmatic public-relations tactic.
